en: The Forty Holy Ones and Khizr Ilyas
Had become his companions.
Abiding beneath blessed fortune,
They charged in ranks of forty.
Against that infidel Sarybai
He charged and thrust his spear.
When Seytek bore down upon him,
The infidel’s fury redoubled—
Your warrior Sarybai,
The boar who devastated the nation,
The villain long accustomed
To drinking blood,
Who had waged war for many years,
Dominated the whole age,
Gnawed down all he encountered,
And, hardened by bloodshed,
Had become renowned as a bloodthirsty killer.
When Seytek leveled his spear,
And drew near
To the field of combat,
“Look, the boy they rely upon
Has come out to fight!
Now I shall settle the account
Of this ill-fated boy
And beat out his ancient madness.
Before he reaches maturity,
Before his coming day can dawn,
I shall finish him altogether.
I shall see the full courage
Of this boy who boasts of strength,
And carefully spill his blood.
I shall curb his imperious rage
And quench him like a dying fire.
Ravening as I wreak havoc,
I shall crush whoever assails me;
I shall leave none around me alive,
And seize him by both skirts.
You wretch who boasts of courage and lionhood,
Who boasts of strength,
I shall put an end to you indeed.
I shall unleash upon this boy
My fierce courage and surpassing fury.
I shall overcome every ailing foe,
Crush whoever encounters me,
Bend down whoever confronts me,
And defeat whoever crosses me.
If I do not conquer their champions,
If I do not swallow all who ride against me,
Then before Sarybai can be called a mighty warrior,
May I sink away unborn;
May I die rather than live!”
They stood opposed to one another,
And Sarybai, enraged,
Roared and leveled his spear.
At the boy, that wolf of war,
He thrust his steel-shafted enchanted spear,
Aiming it at his liver.
A renowned master among spearmen,
A consummate master of cunning,
He had faced heroes in many lands
And met countless disasters as an equal.
The cunning dog knew well how to thrust a spear;
Though the whole world surrounded him, none had defeated him,
And he was a master of stratagems.
When Sarybai thrust his spear,
He gathered all his strength.
When he thunderously drove the spear
At the mighty gray-maned Seytek,
As the spear came for his blood,
And was about to strike its mark,
The spirit-steed Kulansur
Flickered aside like a hare
And darted away like a wild ass.
The arrow-swift, accursed racer
Would not let the spear reach him;
No wind could match his gallop.
The blessed horse was like a spirit of the wind,
And no beast could match his stride.
He flew whirring like an arrow,
And surged like a flying cloud;
A mighty clatter of stones and earth
Whirled above his head.
He bounded as though shot from a bow,
Soft-mouthed and perfectly responsive;
When he turned, he darted aside,
Before one could cry, “This way or that!”
In the blink of an eye,
Before one could say a word,
Before he could turn Tookyzyl’s head,
Before he could steady himself and thrust his spear,
Brave Seytek, upheld by the spirits,
Had already wheeled his horse around.
Before a word could be said,
Before Tookyzyl could close his mouth,
He wheeled about with a shout,
Raising his battle cry,
And before he could thrust at Seytek,
The descendant of the leopard-lion,
The dark-maned, dauntless lion,
The hero of surpassing courage,
Who had ridden into battle there,
Against that mountain-sized villain,
Against that warrior versed in every ruse,
Against that snow-demonic infidel,
Against that mighty, full-blooded champion,
Who deemed himself a hero and a lion,
Who vaunted himself before the whole world,
The matchlessly nimble warrior,
Turned Kulansur’s neck,
And the spear inherited from his forefathers
The heroic prince leveled.
Such was his valor,
His forefather was a mighty, peerless lion,
And there they met in combat.
At the monster-born warrior,
At the infidel who smeared the earth,
“The face of his belt,” he thought,
“The edge of his right shoulder;
If the tempered spear goes lower,
The rim of his ribs;
Here lies the crown of his heart,
His lungs, heart, and windpipe;
If the tempered spear strikes true,
The very core of his heart—
That is the measured mark;
If God wills that it pass through,
His hour of death has come.”
Thus he stood, measuring the spot:
“Support me, my sovereign father;
Straighten whatever swerves,
Guide it true as you desire.”
Such was his consummate skill
As he leveled the wrathful spear,
Straining every sinew,
Hardening himself in fury,
His two strength-giving arms
Gathering all their wondrous power,
His lip bitten through,
His waist bent and body braced,
His rib bones creaking,
His lion eyes flashing,
Swooping like a hawk,
And in that noble lion himself
Unseen wisdom suddenly arose.
The breath from his mouth
Hissed like a speeding bullet,
And the white teeth beneath his brow
Scattered like grains of millet.
The deft lion sprang aside,
And once more within the hero
Unseen wisdom suddenly arose;
He readied himself, spear in hand,
Praying, “O God!”
With matchless agility,
He drove it forward with a sharp crack,
And struck the mountain-huge boar
With a resounding blow.
When he aimed at the measured mark,
When he struck the appointed place,
The tempered spear Bölököñ had made—
Such was that spear:
Torn from a young birch,
Bent true by strongmen,
Perfected by master craftsmen,
Wrapped in mare’s hide,
And hafted by Bölökbay.
Its point had been forged of steel,
So that every man it struck
Would convulse and die,
So that none could retreat,
And whoever met it would know its true nature;
It had been tempered
With human tears.
Along its flank
It was covered with black horsehair,
A tempered spear fit for war,
Forged by Sarybay—
Such was the manner of this strife.
When it found the measured mark,
When it struck the mortal place,
He did not flinch though it rang and rang;
Even when death was at hand,
He counted it less than a trifle.
He neither reeled nor stirred,
The fearsome wrestler, mighty in wrath,
Never budged a hair.
Furious yet unshaken,
Strength and gigantic stature
The Lord Most High had bestowed
Upon that swine without measure.
Without blinking or twitching,
Sarybay stood utterly still.
When Sarybay was pierced,
The ancient tempered steel spear,
The precious heirloom from his father,
Splintered through the middle.
Then the prowess of brave, gray-maned Sarybay
Was made manifest
And revealed before the warriors.
He could shatter any mountain he met,
While the white steed broad as a house
Flew thundering over the plain.
There was no time to ready another spear—
Damn this filthy world!
No other course remained.
When laid to turf it kindled fire;
Whatever it struck died in an instant;
Wherever it landed, blood flowed,
Wherever it slashed, life departed.
Life fled at its stroke:
The Zulfiqar inherited
From gray-maned Manas of old.
Seizing it by the hilt,
Drawing it from its sheath,
He reached him before one could shout, “Strike!”
And with it the noble lion
Slashed once again as he passed.
The other never saw the stroke, not even by a hair;
From the calamity of doom and death,
The swine saw no escape at last.
Roaring in menace,
Bellowing in rage,
Cracking like lightning,
Thunderous as a dragon,
He made every onlooker’s
Whole body shudder.
His wrestler’s form stood revealed
As he girded on his blue-mottled sword,
Sprang like a blue tiger,
Poured out his wrath and ground his teeth;
His attacking arm knotted with power,
His fury made the blood run cold,
And when enraged, misery boiled over.
The accursed monster’s son,
With his cast-iron head broad as a house—
Flee far away if you see his deeds!
He hacked down all who crossed him,
Gnawed apart all he encountered,
Destroyed all he set his eyes upon,
Reduced matchlock-men to ashes,
Filled his quiver with arrows,
And annihilated all who fought him.
That was the deft one, that was the lion,
That was the man endowed with courage.
He turned upon brave Seytek,
Raising his battle-axe and sword
Higher and higher,
His black eyes filling with blood.
His cavernous mouth gaped wide,
And the fire pouring from it
Shot upward toward the sky.
His flesh quivered and his eyes blazed;
His color fled, his arms drew taut.
Parting away in fury,
Terrible in bearing and potent in venom,
He took on the aspect of a dragon.
